rationale: Estragole from another plant oil alters isolated skeletal-muscle contractile responses; it is not tarragon administration or patterned dystonia in a living Parkinson patient.
access_or_open: Original preparation and peripheral assay are documented in linked 1995 extract; a controlled fresh Artemisia dracunculus dystonia comparison remains open. One inherited exact key is an unrelated author surname.

rationale: A 14-person red-perilla extract crossover found 0.24 fewer nighttime voids per night versus starch, with a very low baseline and an inconclusive daytime comparison. A separate oral perilla-extract study prolonged rat void intervals by 27%. Both experiments favor lower void frequency with their tested extracts. The frozen endpoint is the frequency of urgent episodes. Neither source measures urgency, fresh culinary shiso or the response in Parkinson disease.
access_or_open: Patent Table 3 and text disagree on daytime standard error 0.35 versus 0.53. NCT07655219 mixed ginger/perilla dyspepsia registry does not measure urinary urgency; find objective human urgency or fresh-leaf intervention.

rationale: Parkinson constipation handout lists chervil among fiber-containing herbs, but supplies no consumption comparison, preparation-specific exposure or patient bowel outcomes. Chervil-soup allergy case describes acute throat and voice changes, not constipation.
access_or_open: Seek actual fresh Anthriscus cerefolium bowel diary or controlled clinical study; one inherited veterinary dictionary key concerns another chervil name and is resolved.

rationale: UMIN000018516 reports no difference in hoarseness or itching after multiherb Hange-koboku-to versus no formula around intubation; no counts or loudness data and the tested brand or perilla content is not confirmed.
access_or_open: NCT07655219 mixed ginger/perilla product is titled for dyspepsia, despite an inconsistent dysphonia condition field, and lists GI outcomes only; no posted results. Seek isolated dried perilla and acoustic vocal intensity in Parkinson.

rationale: In 19 healthy trained men a seven-day 3 g/day commercial cayenne capsule crossover found no between-treatment difference in fastest or mean 30-m sprint time; gastrointestinal symptom score was 6.3 times higher. Sprint speed and capsule are not everyday walking or a Parkinson trial. Existing chili FFQ study reports composite sarcopenia without a chili-specific walking contrast.
access_or_open: Thesis/product and publication available. Open: measured everyday gait-specific comparisons for ground cayenne in Parkinson; no inference from exercise sprint null.

rationale: Self-selected Parkinson records use ground white mustard alongside broccoli seed in mixed tea; the available selected self-rated symptom records do not report a visual-hallucination-frequency comparison or isolate mustard. Spontaneous patient symptom selection and simultaneous other ingredients prevent inference.
access_or_open: Original report available DOI10.18103/mra.v12i1.4955. Open: underlying symptom item data, ingredient-specific exposure and independent controlled assessment; no hallucination direction is inferred.

rationale: Related isolated cineole or non-cardamom leaf oil experimental motor studies examine induced rodent catalepsy, with different formulations and models; opposing model outcomes cannot be reclassified as dystonia. The cardamom spice review does not supply clinical item-level dystonia data.
access_or_open: Open: original human or PD-study record with ground Elettaria cardamomum and a defined dystonia outcome; published abstract details of PMID31493462 remain limited.

rationale: Intracerebral isolated green-leaf chalcone in 6-OHDA mice improved aggregate behavior; no clinical rigidity or fresh-leaf ingestion. Separate 2024 rotenone mouse perilla seed-oil study improved pole descent, a motor-speed task, and did not measure rigidity.
access_or_open: Original seed-oil body PMC11561828 reviewed in P26 pinky/pmid-pmc.xml; pursue oral fresh-leaf rigidity and registered item-level motor data. Exact scope contains five keys, all dispositioned.

rationale: Parkinson trial assigned encapsulated dried common sage or vitamin E for six weeks, but accessible outcome attachment reports cognition and salivation without handwriting or a timed hand-task estimate; fresh leaves differ.
access_or_open: Secondary-outcome timetable missing from five-page attachment. Two 1988 JNNP scan-only records and two abstract-level pairs still need body checks. The 2014 and 2015 pharmacy guideline bodies resolve two prior access gaps; synthetic SAGE-324 and SAGE publisher are not Salvia exposure.

rationale: In 657 acute cystitis patients the mixed lovage-root, rosemary and centaury preparation and fosfomycin each lowered typical-symptom scores from about 10 to 2 by day 8; the urgency severity plot is a mixed-formula, infection-specific result without dried leaf attribution.
access_or_open: Supplementary Table 4 was inaccessible per local note; seek leaf-only preparation and urgency episode counts in Parkinson rather than inferring efficacy from the root mixture.

rationale: Four PD cases received sequential lemongrass-oil inhalation and massage; clear-writing difficulty ratings remained 0, 0, 1 and 1 across phases. Questionnaire does not measure letter size, oil is nonoral and botanical species not established.
access_or_open: Seek oral brewed Cymbopogon citratus with measured letter size or validated handwriting kinematics and an appropriate comparator; no corresponding inherited keys.

rationale: Phillips 2018 ketogenic and low-fat diets list thyme as a seasoning, with cooked dishes and unspecified species/freshness. UPDRS II total contains handwriting but no item-level estimates, ingredient intake or isolated thyme contrast.
access_or_open: Retrieve individual handwriting items and actual thyme diaries if available; meals confound attribution and UPDRS handwriting is broader than observed letter-size severity. No corresponding inherited keys.

rationale: Randomized older-women trial used powdered ginger in water; hypertensive SBP changed 145.82→142.54 mmHg on ginger versus 150.00→147.30 on control, similar changes. It measures resting pressure, no standing challenge or lightheadedness; grating and Parkinson status do not match. In an independent 22-man meal study, ginger was finely chopped and serial BP was measured; standing symptom was not assessed.
access_or_open: Full primary sources available. Open: verified standing BP and symptom comparison after grated ginger in PD; no automatic inference from a change in resting BP.

rationale: Parkinson Sargol powder tablet study planned MDS-UPDRS Part II, which includes item 2.2 saliva/drooling; an item assessment or total cannot establish a measured item-specific effect. Related 8-week saffron trial abstract reports MDS-UPDRS I item 3 and Part III rather than drooling.
access_or_open: Open: retrieve original trial results or supplement containing item 2.2 by arm and time; ascertain whether actual supplement and culinary grinding match.

rationale: Closest PD signal: observational MVP self-reported coconut-oil use/frequency associated with lower composite PRO-PD symptom scores in overlapping cohorts; no urinary-urgency/frequency-specific coefficient and no virgin-grade confirmation. Separate MS pilot combined 60 mL coconut oil with EGCG and measured anxiety/function/IL-6, not urinary urgency. No defensible direction for urinary urgency/frequency. Open: identify any oil-specific urinary questionnaire item/analysis in the MVP source tables and any human protocol/results with urinary urgency as endpoint; do not infer from composite score.
access_or_open: Full-text contextual reviews confirmed coconut oil and urgency hits belong to separate passages/cohorts; exact pair dispositions are recorded in P26 all-pairs.tsv. Exposure grade and endpoint-specific estimates remain unavailable.

rationale: Two healthy-adult odor experiments found higher saliva secretion after pepper oil. One mixed whole-pepper and capsaicin care case reported increased drooling with inseparable exposures. Clinical drooling depends on saliva clearance as well as secretion. The available studies give no defensible direction for eating cracked pepper in Parkinson disease.
access_or_open: Noh first page and abstract available, full table and exact between-arm estimates unresolved. UMIN000054347 lists results published and 30 enrolled but citation and values are missing; targeted Japanese searches found no identifier-matched paper.

rationale: A topical cinnamon patch improved the urgency item in overactive bladder, and high-dose oral cassia powder reduced voids in chemical cystitis mice. Daytime frequency was inconclusive in the patch trial. In a separate oral cinnamon rat study the bladder-distension response fell with cystitis and rose in controls. The dose, route and condition differences leave the direction of ground cinnamon for Parkinson urgency unresolved.
access_or_open: Original trial and registration available; open original item-level urgency results for oral culinary cinnamon in Parkinson and replication. Favorable topical/induced-model signals compete with an adverse intact-animal response, and do not quantify a directional estimate for this claim.

rationale: Closest hand-function observations are one cervical-myelopathy case with a topical essential-oil blend carried in macadamia oil (grip 17.8 kg at week 1 to 27.3 kg at week 8; no fine-dexterity score) and one carpal-tunnel case with qualitative writing/coin-pickup/clothespin improvement during a blended topical protocol. Neither isolates macadamia oil or confirms cold pressing; no Parkinson dexterity estimate. The oral rat macadamia/soybean diet study measured fatty-acid pharmacodynamic markers, not hand function. No defensible direction for the claim. Open: find human Parkinson-specific pegboard/tapping/handwriting data or isolated macadamia exposure and verify preparation.
access_or_open: Dated local primary summaries available; source pathways are a single case and blended intervention. No inherited exact P26 pairs for 0921; not a zero-result conclusion.

rationale: Observational PD subgroup of 13 participants with genetic variants shows plasma piperine versus total motor score r=-0.466, p=.108; pepper exposure source and dose are not verified, and no hand-specific dexterity score is reported. Total motor correlation cannot establish ground-pepper hand change.
access_or_open: Open: original item-level finger tapping, dexterity testing or ingredient-identified PD exposure with an appropriate comparison; distinguish piperine and whole-pepper forms.

rationale: No macadamia-oil dysphagia endpoint surfaced in dated catalog. Closest macadamia clinical symptom report is a whole-nut ice-cream allergy case with acute excessive drooling/anaphylaxis in a child, not a swallowing assessment or oil exposure. Oil-containing texture experiments evaluate rheology/softness of formulated foods, not patient dysphagia, aspiration or macadamia alone. No direction for cold-pressed macadamia oil and PD dysphagia. Open: search clinical swallowing studies and food texture formulas for macadamia oil; keep whole-nut allergy distinct from expressed oil.
access_or_open: Catalog review surfaced neither an inherited exact P26 pair for 0935 nor a verified oil-only swallowing study. This is scoped absence, not evidence of no effect.

rationale: Closest night-sleep lead is RRIPP-3, where macadamia-oil capsules were the active comparator to krill oil in trainees; no inert/no-oil group and no clear group differences in sleep-related measures, with no insomnia-severity endpoint. Separate 8 g macadamia-oil bread meals in healthy adults reduced acute postmeal sleepiness/fatigue versus controls in the same two-experiment family; this is daytime somnolence, not insomnia, and cold pressing is unverified. No direction for Parkinson insomnia. Open: verify original RRIPP-3 sleep tables/insomnia measurement and any Parkinson-specific insomnia outcomes attributable to oil.
access_or_open: Cochrane full text shows macadamia as comparator vehicle, with suicide/affect/PTSD/cognition outcomes; insomnia references are unrelated. Catalog includes protocol and primary reports, but no cold-pressed PD insomnia endpoint.

rationale: Closest PD human lead: a 2-week multi-food menu including unspecified pumpkin seed oil (with walnut, sesame and olive oils); 16 participants with PD, composite UPDRS III reported at follow-up, no oil-specific assignment/intake or separate handwriting/micrographia measure. Other nearby pumpkin-oil motor reports are animals and use non-micrographia outcomes (e.g., isolated compound stride or stress behavior); no defensible micrographia direction. Open: seek any primary human trial/task with writing size or oil-specific exposure, and verify any prospective result; cold-pressed preparation remains unsupported.
access_or_open: Local catalog summaries link primary Hegelmaier menu/supplement and Pathan figure source. No exact P26 inherited pair for 0977; absence here is not a zero-result search. Oil preparation/amount and handwriting outcome not measured in closest PD study.

rationale: Closest endpoint match is two uncontrolled cases of benign essential blepharospasm (focal dystonia) using topical frankincense; cottonseed, almond or coconut oil may have been diluent, but the report does not map oil to person/outcome. The improvement described is attributable only to the mixed frankincense/botulinum history, not almond oil; no direction for cold-pressed almond oil. A rat 6-OHDA study used almond oil as carrier for CoQ10 plus atorvastatin and measured cardiovascular reflexes, not dystonia. Open: map diluent per case if full text/table permits and search independent almond-only dystonia exposure; oral/cold-pressed grade unverified.
access_or_open: Full text/primary case local summary and 2026 dissertation/article family summarized in dated catalog. P26 review identified almond carrier and unrelated dystonia passages in reviews, not paired outcomes.

rationale: Topical sesame oil in knee osteoarthritis met a reported noninferiority comparison for an eight-meter walk. Oral sesame seeds with standard care produced a post-treatment Timed Up and Go difference. Several other routes involve injected or rectal oil. The 2024 congress item reports the same 15-person Parkinson cohort as the 2017 comparison. No study compared cold-pressed sesame oil consumed for Parkinson walking slowness.
access_or_open: Local primary/abstract summaries anchor sources (PMIDs 31780006, 24164846; 2017 Pathak conference record); no numeric gait effect sizes or oil pressing specs in accessible abstracts. Full 2024 proceedings collection body was screened and shown duplicate.
